clues.description: Inside the chamber, fungal speech changes when channels are rerouted, demonstrating association with flow rather than a resident speaker.

clues.title: A dead guide's route ending at old terrain
clues.description: A convincing voice directs listeners to a river bend that no longer exists beyond the glass, revealing preserved observation rather than present awareness.

clues.title: Living soil beneath the old burn
clues.description: The soil road is darkest and most biologically active where an earlier narrow fire scar crosses it.

clues.title: White fire, opened coats
clues.description: Hard black shells split only in the cooled strip behind the low blackgrass front; unburned shells remain sealed.
clues.discovery: compare shells before and behind the bounded edge

clues.title: New flexible roots behind charred tissue
clues.description: The chamber wall shows young root bands growing beneath old blackened scars.

clues.title: Complete but sealed knots without heat
clues.description: Several crown knots contain soil, light, water, and fungal course but cannot open where the heat current is absent.

clues.title: Oil gives the fire another road
clues.description: At Red Dusk, the low white front stays inside the old scar until it touches the spice sheen; there it climbs rope and canvas, while the same flame dies against wet living soil.
clues.discovery: watch the first flame reach the wagon spill

clues.title: Slack ropes during the deep pulse
clues.description: Lines tied across separate roots go loose only during one long central exhalation.

clues.title: Voice cords relaxing at Root Night
clues.description: Pale cords lose tension together when the Bearer breathes, then draw tight enough to cut soft material.

clues.title: Flame crossing the crownward gap on the exhale
clues.description: The controlled burn can pass a normally closed seam only when the long central exhale opens it.

clues.title: One slack seam between two hard states
clues.description: The crown feeder loosens through the long exhale, then tightens from east to west as the inward draw begins.
clues.discovery: hold a measuring cord across the feeder through the full cycle

clues.title: An old torn knot beside a clean separation scar
clues.description: The crown preserves both a ragged cut made under tension and a smooth socket formed during an earlier breath.

clues.title: Glass hardening after the final exhale
clues.description: At dawn, crown stems become rigid from east to west as soon as the long central exhale ends.

clues.title: Sio's six lines describing one process
clues.description: The old fragment names ground, dawn, rain, memory, fire, and loosening in sequence rather than describing a fruit tree.

clues.title: Soil mist leaving the road
clues.description: Delivered old ground becomes a fine living mist drawn toward the crown instead of remaining as a harvested object.

clues.title: Pollen current without a seed tree
clues.description: Captured dawn leaves many flowers and converges elsewhere, with no single plant bearing the final knot.

clues.title: Several basin branches feeding one lattice
clues.description: Warm rain from distinct pools joins above the roots rather than entering one parent tree.

clues.title: A chosen course entering an unfinished knot
clues.description: Fungal route patterns alter the shape of a translucent crown knot as they arrive.

clues.title: Heat completing only prepared shells
clues.description: The burn opens knots that already contain other currents and destroys empty shells exposed too early.

clues.title: Every missing path leaves a different wound
clues.description: An unfinished knot may be pale, dark, dry, wandering, sealed, or rigid, and each defect traces back to one absent incoming path.
clues.discovery: compare several knots against the six feeders

clues.title: The blocked delivery below the wreck
clues.description: The wagon scar diverts enough soilbearers that only one crownward stream remains supplied.

clues.title: Mist after the first demand is met
clues.description: Once the nearest receiver fills, restored gates continue passing old-ground mist into two farther crown channels.
clues.discovery: hold the repaired road through one complete receiver cycle

clues.title: A restored corridor carrying both soil and heat
clues.description: A protected repaired road lets living ground arrive before bounded fire passes, producing several heat-ready shells.

clues.title: Multiple crown channels opening under balanced burden
clues.description: After the blocked road is relieved, the Bearer opens more than one crownward channel during breath.

clues.title: Several maturing knots after living-soil delivery
clues.description: The crown forms multiple complete knots only when restored old ground arrives alive; without it, one viable knot consumes the remaining flow.

clues.title: One cloud leaves; one cloud travels
clues.description: After the carried seed clears the service root, another mature knot remains attached and cycling while soilbearers still pass living ground into the crown.
clues.discovery: watch the carried seed and the attached crown through one return

events.title: Thirteen Names Beyond the Roots
events.attendance_note: All four roster members present; Hessa labels their report line the Saltward Four.
events.opening_note: The forest has lifted the Cairnroad camp. Orra commissions one people-first survey and requires burden-specific route reports.

events.party_label: The Saltward Four with Orra, Hessa, Nahl, and Sio

events.text: Hessa confirms forty-two names: twenty-nine at camp and thirteen missing among three wagon pockets.
Ansel marks the broad western salt shelf as a provisional walking route but refuses to certify wagon capacity before seeing its moving edge.
Shai treats Sio's six lines as a testable process description, not proof that a removable seed exists.

events.note: Three wagon bells answer from the northeast fork; the rescue party can follow a named sound rather than search the whole moving forest.
Loaded beetles and living pellets identify a crownward road whose traffic is distinct from the caravan wreck.
Closed shining cups above the camp provide a physical locator for the stored-light region.
Upward-traveling droplets reveal a suspended water route rather than ordinary dew.
The smoke front moves west relative to fixed branches and will intersect the wagon scar.
The shrinking salt contact identifies the final ordinary western footing.
The opposing loaded and empty streams show transport between source and receiver.

events.text: Orra opens three parallel work lines: people-first rescue, western-route marking, and observation that may continue only while reports and carriers remain available.

events.party_label: The Saltward Four with Tasa, Rua, Kol, Kesh's handlers, and two litter crews

events.text: Ansel and Kesh name people, load, route, means, and abandonment separately for each of the three pockets.
Len records the spice wagon frame and Pelen's frame as different ownership from Ira's copper stock.
The group hears no responsive person in the fresh cord repetition because it does not stop to test Tovan's copied voice after reaching Tovan alive.

events.note: A repeated well depth fades along a pale cord leading away from the low hollow.
Separate wagon pockets rise together on one warm central pressure cycle.
Sustained eastward motion and the reflected eastern plain make the dawn crossing a present deadline, not merely Sio's inherited warning.

events.text: Upper wheel: Tovan, Deme, Salen, and Miri are lowered alive; the spice frame is cut, two chests are recovered, one chest remains aboard, and the leaking oil jar is caught before it reaches the soil track.

Split freight bed: Pelen is freed with his leg stabilized for carried movement; Bell and most copper pipe reach the western half, while Pelen's frame and several fittings are committed to later repair.
Low hollow: Jun, Iri, Mael, and Daro reach the western climb using Thistle's litter and the handbarrow; Crook is recovered, while Moth and Reed remain loose toward the warm basins.
All forty-two people are physically accounted for before Red Dusk. Nobody dies; Pelen, Lio, Sen, and Daro require carried or assisted movement.

events.party_label: The Saltward Four with Pelen, Ira, Nahl, Vara, and a company repair crew

events.text: Pelen directs from a litter while Len distinguishes his surrendered frame from Ira's lent copper.
Shai checks both the crownward receiver and the neighboring rain acceptance after each repair test.
The party does not follow the reflected-heat turn far enough to use it as a separate verge clue.

events.note: The wreck demonstrably reduced delivery, and a repaired burden-and-gate test produces old-ground mist beyond the first knot's demand.

events.text: The oil break is caught and covered; company canvas and Pelen's dismantled frame carry two opposed beetle streams without crushing them.
Ira lends one pipe length for a reversible scent-rill. The length remains installed in the forest; Len records owner, measure, purpose, and witnesses rather than calling it a gift.
The paired gates pass approach, burden, exhale, and receiver tests. Living old-soil delivery becomes strong and produces surplus crownward mist.
A wet old-ground margin is prepared where the blackgrass heat will cross the repaired corridor.

events.closing_note: All people are accounted for, the soil road is strong, six animals are reduced to two still missing, and the Saltward Four return with distinct rescue, property, route, and seed-process reports.

events.title: Water That Climbs
events.attendance_note: All four present; Pelen participates from a litter and Jun joins the animal-recovery line.
events.opening_note: Outer roots draw inward. The party divides between captured light, the rising basins, and the pale cords before those regions move beyond ordinary access.

events.party_label: Shai and Len with Nahl, Della, and two canopy climbers

events.text: Shai and Len compare intact, dry, and severed-looking cups without cutting a living flower for proof.
The group tracks pollen to a receiver and tests the neighboring water branch before declaring the light current restored.
Two intact cups are rehung and one wet pollen bridge bypasses a dry branch. The light current becomes working but not strong; one branch remains closed.
No flower is severed. Della's living planters remain at camp, and the canopy repair uses company line, basin water, and intact fallen material.

events.party_label: Ansel, Shai, and Kesh with Jun, Olan, Tess, and a water crew

events.text: Kesh and Jun follow Moth and Reed by the pair's upward hoofprints rather than driving another animal into the basin route.
Shai marks one measured cup and checks cooling roots, fungal cords, lantern stems, and the crownward branch before authorizing drinking from replenished yield.

events.note: Captured dawn travels as living pollen through lit water toward the crown; ordinary illumination is not the same function.
Distinct mineral and pollen traces join at one high lattice rather than at a parent tree.
Marked water returns through multiple dependencies; removing the basin contents would weaken the same circuit that replenishes them.
Ground, light, and water arrive from separate sources at one receiver, confirming that the seed is assembled through relations rather than harvested from one organism.

events.text: Moth and Reed are recovered without injury after a cooled return path and Jun's familiar call are established. They later carry assisted travelers, not experimental loads.
The caravan draws only the measured replenishing yield. The basin circuit remains strong after a capillary bypass restores the pinched lower return.
Two casks are filled for immediate departure, but no basin is drained and no water is removed faster than the marked cup returns.

events.party_label: Shai and Len with Sio, Nahl, and Bera as returning courier

events.text: Shai and Sio test a fresh fragment with a new question, then compare repeated measurements across different cadences.
The party selects a course by fall, storage, ground, overflow, and interval rather than by the familiarity of a voice.

events.note: Measurements persist across changing voices and personal details, while a fresh fragment cannot answer a new question.

events.text: A Merewash-compatible course is selected with moderate fall, deep seasonal storage, porous mineral ground, a broad overflow margin, and a long dry interval.
The course is carried forward in one living braid. A wet transcription is sent west as a record but is not treated as the functioning memory current.
The remembered-course current becomes strong enough to preserve one alternate measurement when the crown is diagnosed.

Orra sends the first willing walking group to the western staging ground, but retains sufficient carriers, handlers, and repair workers for Root Night. Ela leaves the inner camp without endorsing the seed attempt.

events.closing_note: All six draft animals are recovered. Soil and rain are strong, captured dawn is working, a living river course is prepared, and the caravan has begun a staged western muster without treating departure as one collective vote.

events.title: One Long Breath
events.attendance_note: All four present; the caravan is divided between departure staging, fire margins, chamber work, and crown preparation.
events.opening_note: Root Night opens the Bearer's service seams. The bounded burn, burden correction, crown descent, and single deep exhale must be coordinated without collapsing into one group action.

events.party_label: Ansel and Len with Pelen, Rusk, Vara, and two margin crews

events.text: Ansel requires two maintained margins, a prepared receiver, and a named retreat before allowing each segment to advance.
Len records the remaining spice chest as abandoned property rather than fuel; Rusk's caught oil is carried west before ignition.

events.note: Narrow earlier scars preserve active soil, prepared shells open behind bounded heat, and empty shells exposed too early fail.

events.text: The wagon-scar and restored-corridor segments pass low between wet old-ground margins. Soil delivery continues before and after the heat front.
The crownward seam is held at its prepared edge until the deep exhale. Bounded heat is working; runaway fire remains absent.
One dry canvas strip is spent as an outer warning margin. The fire never reaches the rescued wagon line or the lantern pollen bridge.

events.party_label: Kesh and Shai with Nahl, Tobin, Corda, and a burden crew

events.text: The chamber team maps western carry, middle circulation, and crownward lift burdens separately.
Kesh refuses to use Bell and Crook as a forced test load; dismantled wagon material provides the reversible burden instead.
Shai restores the cooling path before the preliminary breath is used to check the service-root redirection.

events.note: Both heat passage and direct stem observation identify one long central slack interval followed by immediate hardening.

events.text: The western carry band is relieved by moving the abandoned axle and committed frame pieces onto the middle support band.
The middle circulation band is cooled and remains open. The crownward lift band balances after the restored soil stream enters under burden.
One preliminary breath confirms the service root and wet middle ledge without spending the unique deep exhale. Root pulse becomes working and the deep-exhale window remains unused.

events.party_label: The Saltward Four with Nahl, Sio, Jun, Pelen, and the crown and verge crews

events.text: The crown group reads missing currents from separate knot defects before assigning labor to any repair.
Shai distinguishes a clean socket test from the separate evidence needed to call one knot surplus.
Len records the wet cradle, seed custodian, continuing soil delivery, attached mature knot, and fire state before separation begins.

The working light branch is directed to the selected receiver; strong soil, strong rain, the living course, bounded heat, and balanced root pulse complete two mature knots and one viable unopened knot.
During the long central exhale, the crownward seam receives bounded heat, the selected mature knot completes its return, and a wet cradle bears its weight before the feeder ring is drawn free.
One mature surplus seed separates with a smooth living socket. One other mature knot and one viable knot remain attached; living-soil delivery continues and no common return is lost.
The carried seed contains the Merewash-compatible course and begins transport in a closed wet cradle under Shai and Nahl's joint custody.

events.closing_note: The deep exhale is spent exactly once. A clean mature surplus seed is in its cradle, one mature knot remains attached, and departure crews move under the inward draw toward the Glass Verge.

events.title: The Last Salt
events.attendance_note: All four present at opening; the session ends with all four west of the verge and two recorded voluntary eastbound travelers.
events.opening_note: First reflection has passed. Crown work and three burden-specific departures now resolve in parallel before direct sun removes ordinary western footing.

events.party_label: The Saltward Four, Orra's last departure crews, and the two eastbound volunteers

events.text: Ansel states each route by burden and closing sign. Hessa reads every name before the inward draw.
Sio and Jun separately hear the westward options, eastbound exposure, available supplies, and possible nonreturn before choosing continued migration.
The party does not use the obsolete dead-guide route or the distant wagon silhouette as new evidence; both opportunities are recorded as missed.
The broad salt shelf carries the first walking group, dependents, most hand loads, Clove and Sedge, and one surviving camp wagon before the retreating edge narrows.
The wet middle ledge carries the mature seed cradle, Shai, Nahl, Bell and Crook under Rua and Tess, and the carried or assisted travelers Pelen, Lio, Sen, and Daro.
The crown service root carries Orra, Hessa, Ansel, Kesh, Len, the final route keepers, Moth and Reed, and the remaining records before the inward draw closes it.

Forty people reach the western salt alive. Sio Tern and Jun Alder remain aboard by separately recorded choice with water, grain, blankets, tools, course transcriptions, and a named plan to observe the forest beyond the Glass Waste.
All forty-two people are accounted for: forty westbound, two eastbound, none unresolved, none dead. All six missing draft animals and Thistle are westbound.

The westbound caravan retains two spice chests, most copper pipe, Merewash seed grain, reservoir tools, medicinal planters, water casks, and dismantled loads; the spice wagon, grain wagon, Pelen's frame, one pipe length, and several fittings remain with the forest.

The carried knot is a mature surplus seed, cleanly separated and still circulating. The forest continues east with one mature knot attached, one viable knot, strong soil and rain, working light, strong remembered course, working bounded heat, working root pulse, and no runaway fire.

Ira ratifies the emergency pipe use but leaves compensation open. Pelen confirms his frame as a voluntary repair contribution. The abandoned spice and grain property remain named claims rather than disappearing into the successful outcome.

events.closing_note: Direct sun closes western footing. The caravan, seed, animals, records, and forty westbound people stand on the White Salt; Sio and Jun continue east as known volunteers rather than missing persons.
